name: Pewter-Shroud
geological_features: Perpetual fog banks fed by low-altitude cloud layers
Rolling hills of grey mineral-rich soil
Subterranean ocean beneath the northern continent
specific_features: Colony settlement established by fog-adapted settlers
description: Pewter-Shroud lives up to its name: a world swathed in permanent grey mist that softens every edge and muffles every sound. The terrain is a rolling expanse of gentle hills covered in pewter-colored moss and low scrubland, broken by dark lakes that appear and vanish in the shifting fog. The sky is an undifferentiated grey dome, its sun visible only as a brighter smear of light that tracks slowly overhead.

The fog carries a faintly sweet, mineral scent that clings to clothing and skin long after departure. Sound behaves strangely here, sometimes carrying voices across kilometers, sometimes swallowing a shout at arm's length. The fauna has adapted to this low-visibility world, developing echolocation and bioluminescent markings that create ghostly trails of light moving through the mist.

Early settlers chose this world precisely for its obscurity, establishing small communities that remain nearly invisible to orbital surveys. Over generations, the colonists have adapted to the perpetual twilight, developing enhanced hearing and a social structure built around acoustic communication. The subterranean ocean beneath the northern continent remains largely unexplored, though sonar readings suggest vast cavern systems that may harbor their own ecosystems.

Pewter-Shroud serves as a waystation for those who prefer not to be found, and its fog-shrouded settlements ask few questions of visitors. The planet's medicinal mosses have proven effective against several degenerative conditions, creating a quiet but lucrative export trade. However, recent reports of unfamiliar bioluminescent patterns in the deep fog have unsettled even the most stoic residents, suggesting something new is moving through the mist.
